question.text: According to the US SEC, High Frequency Trading (HFT) is characterized by all of the following features EXCEPT __________.

answer.text: Positions are typically held for several weeks to capture medium-term price trends
Use of extraordinarily fast and sophisticated computer programs for generating, routing, and executing orders
Very short holding periods, often measured in minutes or seconds
Very high order-to-trade ratios from rapid order entry and removal

explanation.text: The Logic: Per p125, the US SEC defines HFT by these features: fast and sophisticated programs for generating, routing and executing orders; very small holding periods (minutes or seconds); very high order-to-trade ratios from rapid order entry/removal; and closing most positions by the end of the day. Holding positions for several weeks contradicts these features. The Trap: All three incorrect options are actual HFT features per the p125 SEC definition. The keyed option (positions held for weeks) directly contradicts the very short holding periods and end-of-day flat characteristic. Note: Any reference to holding for days or weeks rules out HFT under the SEC definition on p125.
